questions.question:
**Direction: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I could have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **could have​.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Conditional sentences are statements discussing known factors or hypothetical situations and their consequences.
 
• One of the structures is mentioned below:
 
• This particular type is followed when something didn't happen as a certain condition wasn't fulfilled.
 
 
• If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.
 
• Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (alternative structure)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would had call you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would have called you.***
 
• *Had I noticed you, I would have called you.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] 
 
 
 
• To follow the given structure correctly, **'would have' **will replace** 'could have' **in the part given in the** 3rd option.**

 

Correct Sentence__: *Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I **would have **certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• There is one more type of conditional sentence in the past tense given below:
 
• This particular type is followed when we talk about something in the past which is purely imaginary.
 
 
• If + Simple Past, Subject + Would + V1 + Object.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *If I had wings, I would fly like a bird.*
 
 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__***

__
 
• **सशर्त वाक्य (conditional sentence)** ज्ञात कारकों या काल्पनिक स्थितियों और उनके परिणामों पर चर्चा करने वाले बयान हैं।
 
• संरचनाओं में से एक का उल्लेख नीचे किया गया है:
 
• इस विशेष प्रकार का पालन तब किया जाता है जब कुछ नहीं हुआ क्योंकि एक निश्चित शर्त पूरी नहीं हुई थी।
 
 
• **If + Subject + had + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object.**
 
• **Had + Subject + been + V3 + object, Subject + Would have + V3 + Object. (वैकल्पिक संरचना)**
 
 
 
• उदाहरण:
 
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would had call you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *If I had noticed you, I would have called you.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
• *Had I noticed you, I would have called you.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] 
 
 
 
• दी गई संरचना का सही ढंग से पालन करने के लिए, तीसरे विकल्प में दिए गए भाग में 'could have' के स्थान पर 'would have' होगा।

 ​

**सही वाक्य: ***Had you told me that you were in Mumbai I would have certainly contacted you instead of waiting here.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• नीचे दिए गए भूत काल में एक और प्रकार का सशर्त वाक्य (conditional sentence) है:
 
• इस विशेष प्रकार का अनुसरण तब किया जाता है जब हम अतीत में किसी ऐसी चीज के बारे में बात करते हैं जो विशुद्ध रूप से काल्पनिक है।
 
 
• If + Simple Past, Subject + Would + V1 + Object.
 
 
 
• उदाहरण:
 
 
• *If I had wings, I would fly like a bird.*

questions.question:

Have several irons in the fire

options.text: Having too many engagements at a time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Having too many engagements at a time​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the given idiom:

 
 
• **Have several irons in the fire**- to be involved with many activities or jobs at the same time or to make certain that there are always several possibilities available (एक ही समय में कई गतिविधियों या नौकरियों में शामिल होना या यह सुनिश्चित करना कि हमेशा कई संभावनाएं उपलब्ध हों)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *If that job application doesn't work out I've got **a couple more irons in the fire.***
 
 

​* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Let's look at the origin of the idiom:

 
 
• The expression **too many irons in the fire** are derived from the trade of **blacksmithing**. (आग में बहुत अधिक लोहे की अभिव्यक्ति लोहार के व्यापार से ली गई है।)
 
• If a blacksmith attempts to heat** too many pieces of iron** in his fire at once, it cools the fire and none of the pieces of iron will heat properly. (यदि लोहार अपनी आग में लोहे के बहुत से टुकड़े एक साथ गर्म करने का प्रयास करता है, तो वह आग को ठंडा कर देता है और लोहे का कोई भी टुकड़ा ठीक से गर्म नहीं होगा।)
 
• The phrase too many irons in the fire dates back to the **mid-1500s. **(आग में बहुत अधिक बेड़ी का वाक्यांश 1500 के दशक के मध्य का है।)
